subtitle: How a Satrap’s Count of Years Became India’s Quiet Clock

panels.shot: low-angle dramatic wide of a stone inscription glowing against a starry sky, numbers etched deep while Chashtana’s silhouette looms behind
panels.action: Chashtana stands in shadow behind a great rock-face inscription, his figure half-lit by torchlight as chisel-marks of numerals shimmer like a new constellation under a vast night sky.

dialogue.text: In 78 CE, a satrap named Chashtana began to count his years—and that count still beats, unseen, inside India’s national calendar.

i18n.hi: ७८ ईस्वी में चष्टन नाम के एक क्षत्रप ने अपने साल गिनने शुरू किए — वही गिनती आज भी भारत के राष्ट्रीय पंचांग के भीतर धड़क रही है।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over western India, sweeping from desert coast to inland city
panels.action: A vast aerial view shows the dry coasts of Kutch, caravans threading the salt flats, and inland, the clustered roofs and temple spires of Ujjain under a hazy sun.

dialogue.text: Western India, first century of the Common Era—ports at Kutch, caravans over salt plains, and inland cities like Ujjain humming with trade and ritual time.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी भारत, पहली सदी — कच्छ के बंदरगाह, नमक मैदानों पर कारवाँ, और उज्जैन जैसी नगरियाँ, जहाँ व्यापार और पूजा की घड़ियाँ साथ बजती हैं।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Chashtana in a council hall, lit by oil lamps
panels.action: Chashtana sits on a modest satrapal throne in a pillared hall, scrolls and palm-leaf documents before him, councillors on either side as shadows flicker on stone walls.

dialogue.text: Here ruled the Western Kshatrapas, Saka satraps of foreign steppe stock, now long rooted in this land; among them rose Chashtana, son of Ghsamotika.

i18n.hi: यहाँ पश्चिमी क्षत्रप राज करते थे — विदेशी स्तेपी से आए शक शासक, जो अब इसी मिट्टी में जड़ थे; इन्हीं में से उठा घसमोटिकपुत्र चष्टन।

panels.shot: close-up on Chashtana studying coins and tablets
panels.action: At a stone desk, Chashtana leans forward, studying a mix of silver coins and wooden writing tablets, his brows knit as he traces markings with a calloused finger.

dialogue.text: He ruled not with mythic thunder, but with metal, record and tax; his power flowed through coins, land-grants and dates scratched into stone.

i18n.hi: उसने न देवताओं की गर्जना से, बल्कि धातु, लेख और कर से राज किया; उसका बल सिक्कों, भूदानों और पत्थरों पर खुदी तिथियों से बहता था।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot as Chashtana looks at priests and scribes arguing before him
panels.action: Facing Chashtana, a Brahmin priest with a palm-leaf almanac and a Greek-cloaked scribe with a wax tablet gesture in different directions, each pointing to a different date scheme.

dialogue.text: Across his realm, dates clashed—old local eras, regnal counts, lunar months, Greek-style reckonings brought by earlier kings.

i18n.hi: उसकी भूमि में तिथियाँ भिड़ती थीं — पुराने स्थानीय युग, राजाबदोश साल, चांद्र मास, और पहले राजाओं के लाए यूनानी हिसाब।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Chashtana in thought, light catching one eye
panels.action: Chashtana sits back in thought, fingers steepled, lamplight catching the sharp line of his cheek and the resolve in his eyes as a map of his territories lies rolled open nearby.

dialogue.speaker: chashtana
dialogue.text: If my writ is to hold, our years must march as one.

i18n.hi: अगर मेरा हुक्म टिकना है, तो हमारे साल एक साथ चलने चाहिए।

panels.shot: symbolic montage wide, calendar glyphs overlaying his figure
panels.action: A stylized image shows Chashtana’s figure superimposed with faint outlines of moons, solar paths, and numeric marks, as lines radiate outward toward stylized forts and temples.

dialogue.text: Some scholars see his answer in a decision: to root his rule in a single era, a new count of years beginning around 78 CE.

i18n.hi: कुछ विद्वान उसकी राह एक फैसले में देखते हैं — अपने राज को एक ही युग में जड़ देना, एक नई साल-गिनती जो करीब ७८ ईस्वी से शुरू होती है।

panels.shot: close-up on a stonecutter’s hands carving numerals into rock
panels.action: A stonecutter’s strong hands press chisel to rock, knocking out neat numerals and letters as dust curls away from the newly carved date line on an inscription slab.

dialogue.text: The modern name is the Saka era. Its year one is fixed by today’s scholars in 78 CE, though the hand that first began it remains debated.

i18n.hi: आज हम इसे शक युग कहते हैं। इसका पहला साल विद्वान ७८ ईस्वी मानते हैं, पर इसे शुरू करने वाला हाथ अब भी विवाद में है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Kutch landscape with an inscription pillar at Andhau
panels.action: In the stark Kutch landscape, an upright inscribed stone at Andhau stands alone amid scrub and rock, the horizon a shimmering line of heat.

dialogue.text: Out at Andhau in Kutch, in this dry country under his sway, two silent stones still bear its ticking years.

i18n.hi: कच्छ के अंदरौ गाँव में, उसकी हुकूमत की इस सूखी धरती पर, दो खामोश पत्थर आज भी उसके सालों की टिक टिक ढो रहे हैं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on the inscription text band where the date appears
panels.action: The camera closes on weathered letters and numerals in the Andhau inscription band, the carved date line standing out where light grazes the stone’s roughness.

dialogue.text: One speaks of year 11 of the Saka era; another, year 52. D. C. Sircar read these numbers as anchors for Chashtana and his line.

i18n.hi: एक पर शक युग का साल ११ खुदा है; दूसरे पर ५२। डी. सी. सिरकार ने इन्हीं अंकों से चष्टन और उसकी वंशरेखा को बाँधा।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of a satrapal court scene dissolving between rulers
panels.action: A court scene dissolves like a faded painting: Chashtana on the throne becomes later satraps in similar poses, while the stone grant they hold remains constant, its date line unchanged.

dialogue.text: Long after his own name fades from many records, Western Kshatrapa grants and coin legends keep using this Saka count, year after year.

i18n.hi: जब उसका नाम कई अभिलेखों से मिटने लगा, तब भी पश्चिमी क्षत्रपों के दानपत्र और सिक्के शक गिनती ही दोहराते रहे, साल दर साल।

panels.shot: split-panel style composition, one side showing a Kushan court, the other a scholar’s desk
panels.action: On one side, a Kushan emperor sits in northern finery; on the other, in a modern study, a historian bends over charts and timelines, books piled high.

dialogue.text: Earlier, many tied this era to Kanishka of the Kushans, seeing his rise as the dawn of 78 CE; recent work, like Harry Falk’s, has loosened that bond.

i18n.hi: पहले, कई लोग इस युग को कुशान सम्राट कनिष्क से जोड़ते थे, मानते थे कि ७८ ईस्वी उसकी चढ़त का सवेरा है; हाल की शोध, जैसे हैरी फाल्क की, ने यह गाँठ ढीली कर दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern scholar turning pages of an epigraphic corpus
panels.action: A present-day scholar in a quiet library turns the pages of a thick volume titled in tiny print with inscriptions, notes and cross-referenced dates scattered across the desk.

dialogue.text: Richard Salomon and others follow the inscriptions themselves: where a date says ‘of the Saka era,’ they track how, where and by which rulers it was used.

i18n.hi: रिचर्ड सालोमन और दूसरे सीधे शिलालेखों का पीछा करते हैं — जहाँ भी लिखा मिलता है ‘शक युग का वर्ष’, वे देखते हैं यह कब, कहाँ, किन राजाओं के नीचे चला।

panels.shot: montage of different inscriptions from western India, their date lines highlighted
panels.action: A montage of stone slabs and copper plates from different sites in western India fills the frame, each with its date line subtly picked out by angled light.

dialogue.text: Across centuries, from these satraps onward, inscriptions in western India quietly mark time ‘by the Saka era,’ even as dynasties rise and fall around them.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक, इन क्षत्रपों से आगे भी, पश्चिमी भारत के अभिलेख चुपचाप समय नापते रहे — ‘शक युग के वर्ष’ में — जबकि राजवंश आते-जाते रहे।

panels.shot: contrast panel showing a bard reciting to a king with imagined heroic scenes behind him
panels.action: A later-age court bard stands before a crowned king, gesturing animatedly as painted scenes behind him show Shalivahana and Vikramaditya in stylized heroic poses.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile, storytellers spin new cycles—Vikramaditya, Shalivahana, heroic foes of ‘Sakas’—weaving the era into legend, but these tales rest in poetry, not in stone dates.

i18n.hi: इसी बीच, कथाकार नए चक्र बुनते हैं — विक्रमादित्य, शालिवाहन, ‘शकों’ के वीर दुश्मन — जो इस युग को दंतकथाओं में पिरोते हैं, पर ये किस्से कविताओं में हैं, पत्थर की तिथियों में नहीं।

panels.shot: modern cityscape of New Delhi with a subtle overlay of calendar pages
panels.action: A wide view of modern New Delhi’s government buildings under a clear sky is overlaid faintly with turning calendar pages marked ‘Saka’ alongside Gregorian dates.

dialogue.text: In the twentieth century, an independent India chooses this same Saka era for its national civil calendar, setting year one at 78 CE once more before the world.

i18n.hi: बीसवीं सदी में, आज़ाद भारत अपने राष्ट्रीय नागरिक पंचांग के लिए इसी शक युग को चुनता है, दुनिया के सामने फिर से साल एक को ७८ ईस्वी पर जमाकर।

panels.shot: close-up of a printed Indian national calendar page showing Saka year alongside CE
panels.action: A close view of a wall calendar shows today’s Gregorian date paired with a neat printed line reading the corresponding Saka year and month in clear typeface.

dialogue.text: Every time those twin dates are printed—a Saka year beside a Common Era one—the long clock that began in 78 CE ticks again, half-seen yet precise.

i18n.hi: जब भी जुड़वाँ तिथियाँ छपती हैं — शक साल के साथ सामने सामान्य युग की तिथि — ७८ ईस्वी में शुरू हुई यह लंबी घड़ी फिर टिकती है, आधी छिपी पर एकदम नाप-तौल।

panels.shot: ghostly overlay of Chashtana’s face over the modern calendar and inscription
panels.action: Chashtana’s calm, weathered face appears as a transparent overlay between a modern calendar and an ancient inscription, his eyes steady, as if watching time stretch across the ages.

dialogue.text: We may never prove whose mind first fixed that epoch, but Chashtana’s age shows how a ruler’s need for order can cast a shadow longer than any throne.

i18n.hi: शायद हम कभी न जान पाएँ कि किस बुद्धि ने वह युग-सीमा पहली बार ठोकी, पर चष्टन का जमाना दिखाता है कि एक शासक की व्यवस्था की चाह उसका राजसिंहासन से कहीं लंबा साया डाल सकती है।

title_i18n.en: The Saka Era Begins Its Long Clock
title_i18n.hi: शक युग की लंबी घड़ी चालू होती है

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Satrap’s Count of Years Became India’s Quiet Clock
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक क्षत्रप के सालों की गिनती कैसे बनी भारत की शांत घड़ी
